findings.where: Step 10 of 15 ('At once, and always live'), the SHOW text
findings.what: The screen carries 98 words (W9's 88 plus 'Drag the fault along the cable, and the trace follows.'), over the ~90-word limit, and it packs two ideas (the current arrives at once; the cells are always live); move the always-live sentences to step 11's Why or cut 'There is no slow build-up to react to.' and 'Here the trace is flat at 1813 A by 5 ms.'

The lesson carries 20 footnote markers (12 in explain, 8 in practice), far over 'at most a few a lesson'; keep them only on values he might look up (the block's 6.95 mΩ and 1814 A, 90% at about 60% charge, 5 to 10 ms, 1.20 V and 3.60 V) and drop the rest.

findings.where: Step 8 of 15 ('Running down'), W7's last sentence and the say line
findings.what: 'At 60% charge, the block here still drives 1668 A' and 'That is 96% of its full-charge fault' state as the real EnerSys block's figures numbers that come from an assumed straight-line sketch (92% at 60%), while the caption says the block is real and nothing on screen says the line is a sketch; say 'in this sketch' or label the band 'sketch: tests stayed over 90%'.

findings.where: Step 10 of 15, the time trace label and say line
findings.what: The trace label 'full by 5 ms' and the say line 'reaches its full 1813 A within 5 ms of the fault' state the sketch's 5 ms as fact, while the text gives the measured 5 to 10 ms; mark the trace as a sketch or say 'within 5 to 10 ms'.

findings.where: Step 12 of 15, chemistry card, Lead-acid 'Main hazard'
findings.what: 'Main hazard: very corrosive acid' for lead-acid is an unsourced ranking that leaves out hydrogen on charge, the explosion risk lesson 5 taught (and nickel-cadmium vented cells gas too); rename the row 'Hazards' and list acid and hydrogen, or drop 'main'.

The 90-word paragraph restates the card's rows almost word for word (cell volts, cells for 24 V, electrolyte, hydrometer, hazard), so the screen reads everything twice; cut the prose to the one idea (same rule, different cells) plus the thermal-runaway meaning and let the card carry the facts.

'That is why a shorted battery can give 100 to 1000 times its normal discharge current' does not follow from the 2553 A on screen because no normal discharge current is given; give the string's everyday current for comparison or drop 'That is why'.

findings.where: Step 4 of 15 ('Down the cable'), SHOW text
findings.what: The screen text is 93 words with the drag instruction, plus a 20-word say line under the slider; cut 'Resistances in series add.' (his trade) to bring it under 90.

findings.where: Step 15 of 15 ('A lithium-ion pack'), picture before Check
findings.what: At 360 px and 1280 px the picture is nearly empty before Check (a title, '? cells' and a dashed 24 V line); draw one 3.60 V cell against the 24 V line so the question has something to look at.

findings.where: Step 14 of 15 ('Can it clear it?'), choices
findings.what: The right choice is the only one carrying a calculation ('No: 25.2 ÷ 0.016 = 1575 A, above 1 kA'), so it can be picked without working; give it as 'No: about 1575 A, above 1 kA' against wrong numeric choices, or keep the sum for the feedback.

findings.where: Step 3 of 15 ('A spanner across it') Why, and explain
findings.what: The lesson never says what a thousand amps does through a spanner (it heats and can melt metal, throws an arc, and a spark can light hydrogen), and the brief promised arc flash named in one line; add one sentence to the spanner Why.
'sealed in the cell' says where the electrolyte is, not what it is; one sourced word on what it is (a flammable organic liquid) would also explain why thermal runaway is its hazard.

'In one test the current reached its full value within 5 to 10 ms' and 'The figures here come from a simplified model' lean on where the facts come from and talk about the lesson itself; say 'The current reaches its full value within 5 to 10 ms' and drop the model line, which the picture's limits already cover.

findings.where: Step 8 W7 and explain ('You saw that on the voltmeter in lesson 2')
findings.what: The back-reference talks about the course rather than the cell; 'A rested cell's voltage falls only a little as its charge goes' stands alone.

findings.where: Step 4 of 15 picture at 360 px light and dark (fault at 15 m)
findings.what: The '15 m' distance label sits tight against the lower core's current chevrons; it reads, but nudge the brace label up a few pixels.
